epic.name: Redesign the expense files view as a batch register
unverifiedAssumptions: The register's section heading 'Submitted files' is now set as a small capitalised tracked label rather than a bold title, matching the column heads below it. That is a judgement about how the screen should read, not something the brief states outright — worth a glance to confirm it looks like a document label rather than a heading that got lost.

AC-1 says the slip must be underlined fields with small capitalised labels and no card, but not how the slip as a whole is bounded. It was read as one ruled field strip closed by a single hairline at its foot — the same shape the request list's narrowing strip has above its listing — rather than each field getting a band of its own. Worth a glance to confirm that is the intended reading of 'the same control-total grammar'.

On the three screens that have no file to show (still loading, file not available, file could not be read), the page's own title 'Submitted file' is now set as a small capitalised label rather than a large page heading — consistent with how the register and the slip label themselves, but a judgement about hierarchy on a screen with nothing else on it.

The file's name is the largest text on its page (about 20px, typewriter face). The brief deliberately forbids a big control-total figure here (BR5), so nothing on the slip is set at display scale — worth an eye against the register it sits beside.
